Systems can use LVs as raw block devices just like disk partitions: creating mountable file systems on them, or using them as swap storage.

Striped LVs allocate each successive LE from a different PV; depending on the size of the LE, this can improve performance on large sequential reads by bringing to bear the combined read-throughput of multiple PVs.

By Lemma 1 the set $A$ is equal to $(A \cap B) \cup (A - B)$. Therefore again with transitivity, the set $(A \cap B) \cup (A \cap (C - B))$ is equal to $(A \cap B) \cup (A - B)$.
